rule: A git or GitHub identifier enters Bash source only captured out of band or after passing the identifier gate
description: `plugin/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline) is the canonical source for the rule that a git or GitHub identifier (branch, base, remote, upstream ref, commit SHA, or PR reference) never enters model-authored Bash source as an unvalidated literal. The rule is load-bearing because double-quoting is not a shell-safety encoding: Bash expands `$(...)`, backticks, and `${...}` from literal bytes in command source even inside double quotes, but never from a variable's contents. The source pin is ONE span carrying both branches of the rule. The out-of-band branch carries its condition (a command can produce the identifier inside the same Bash call) and its obligation (command substitution into a shell variable, referenced only as `"$var"`). The literal branch carries its condition (an identifier must enter command text as a literal, whether supplied by the caller or read from an earlier call's output) and its obligation (it first passes the identifier gate in the agent's OWN reasoning BEFORE that Bash call, and a value that fails stops the procedure with a blocker that does not echo the value). Rewriting either condition or either obligation, including unquoting the variable reference, moving the gate after the Bash call, or dropping the non-echo requirement, turns the suite red. Four consumers in the same file pin the section header `## Shell Identifier Discipline`, which every site pointer names, the identifier-gate definition sentence, the commit SHA sentence that completes that definition, and the trust boundary. The definition is load-bearing because it is the only definition every site validates against: the branch, base, and remote charset `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`, the non-empty, leading `-`, and `..` exclusions, the PR number `^[0-9]+$` and PR URL `^https://[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` classes, and the commit SHA classes `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` and `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, which a reported commit passes before it enters command text as a literal. The trust boundary is load-bearing because it fixes what the rule defends against, so a reviewer can tell a defect from a recorded residual. It is pinned as ONE span carrying its condition (the rule defends against untrusted identifier text only, and repo hooks, local refs, git config, and the operator are trusted) and its obligation (a change those trusted parties make between a check and a write is outside the rule and is recorded as a residual, as in the push-branch script's NOT CHECKED header, not defended against). Adding to or removing from the trusted set, or dropping the residual record, turns the suite red. Seven consumers pin the gate sentence at each application site, each as one span carrying WHICH inputs are gated, the pointer to the canonical file and section, and the failure stop: `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md` gates `head`, `base`, and `push_remote` at its input gate; `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` gates `head`, `base`, and `push_remote` at its input gate, with the stop stating that the blocker echoes no value, the PR number at step 8, and the commit from the step 6 `commit:` line at step 8 as a commit SHA; `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/SKILL.md` gates `base` and `working_branch`; `plugin/skills/gather-facts/SKILL.md` gates `trunk` and, when provided, `remote` against the identifier gate and each reference against the PR number class `^[0-9]+$` with at most 20 references, with the stop stating that the blocker never echoes the value; `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` gates `pr`, `working_branch`, and `base`. Dropping an input from a site's list, retargeting its pointer, or deleting its stop turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these twelve word sequences exist in these six named files; they claim nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that makes a gate optional or permits pasting a value after it passes, is invisible; (2) the site pins are pointer pins and do not prove that any site's commands comply with the rule; the out-of-band command forms are pinned separately, and only the named forms are covered there; (3) a NEW skill or agent that pastes an identifier into Bash source without carrying a gate sentence is an absence defect that no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract, and no structural check for it exists in `tools/policy_check.sh`; (4) the github-reviewer grant wording in `plugin/governance/safety-rails.md` and the charset copies in Brood Spawn Bypass-Mode Mitigation control 3, `hivemind:spawn-brood`, and `hivemind:brood-status` are outside these pins, so they can drift from the identifier-gate definition while the suite stays green; (5) the canonical section's double-quoting explanation and its Consumers line are unpinned; its fresh-shell paragraph (a later Bash call re-derives a captured value rather than pasting it, and a push runs in the same call, or the same committed script, as every check on the ref it writes) and that paragraph's written-identity exception (a later call that verifies an earlier call's write compares against the reported value and never re-derives it) are pinned by the push single-process fixture, not here.

source.pattern: Capture out-of-band whenever a command can produce the identifier inside the same Bash call: command substitution into a shell variable, referenced only as `"$var"`. Any identifier that must enter command text as a literal, whether supplied by the caller or read from an earlier call's output, first passes the identifier gate in the agent's OWN reasoning BEFORE that Bash call, and a value that fails stops the procedure with a blocker that does not echo the value.

consumers.pattern: Identifier gate: a branch, base, or remote name matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`, is non-empty, does not start with `-`, and contains no `..`; a PR reference is a PR number matching `^[0-9]+$` or a PR URL matching `^https://[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`.

This rule defends against untrusted identifier text only. Repo hooks, local refs, git config, and the operator are trusted, so a change they make between a check and a write is outside this rule and is recorded as a residual, as in the push-branch script's NOT CHECKED header, not defended against.

**Input gate.** Before any Bash call, validate `head`, `base`, and, when provided, `push_remote` against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline); on failure, exit 1 with `blocker: head, base, or push_remote contains characters outside the safe allowlist`.

**Input gate.** Before any Bash call, validate `head`, `base` and, when provided, `push_remote` against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline); on failure, exit 1 with `blocker: head, base or push_remote contains characters outside the safe allowlist`, which echoes no value.

Take the PR number from the trailing `/pull/<n>` segment of the step 7 URL and validate it against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline) before the Bash call; on failure, exit 1 with `blocker: PR number contains characters outside the safe allowlist`.

Take the commit from the step 6 `commit:` line and validate it as a commit SHA against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline) before the Bash call; on failure, exit 1 with `blocker: pushed commit is not a full commit SHA`.

**Input gate.** Before any Bash call, validate `base` and `working_branch` against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline); on failure, exit 1 with `blocker: base or working_branch contains characters outside the safe allowlist`.

**Input gate.** Before any Bash call, validate `trunk` and, when provided, `remote` against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline), and each reference against `^[0-9]+$`, with at most 20 references. On failure, exit 1 with `blocker: trunk, remote, or a reference fails the input gate`. The blocker never echoes the value.

Before the step 1 Bash call, validate `pr`, `working_branch`, and `base` against the identifier gate in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline); a value that fails returns `blocked` with `blocker_reason: input outside the safe identifier allowlist`.
